events.title: Federal judge orders hearing on selective prosecution of human smuggling defendant
events.summary: AP reported on December 26 that a federal judge canceled Kilmar Abrego Garcia's trial for human smuggling charges and instead ordered a hearing to determine whether Abrego Garcia's prosecution was sought vindictively in an effort to selectively target him. If prosecutors fail to explain their reasoning for charging Abrego Garcia, the charges against him could be dismissed.
events.why_relevant: The court's scrutiny of selective prosecution protects against weaponization of the justice system for political purposes; later reporting revealed DOJ leadership involvement in the charging decision.
events.basis: A federal judge canceled Kilmar Abrego Garcia's trial for human smuggling charges and instead ordered a hearing to determine whether Abrego Garcia's prosecution was sought vindictively in an effort to selectively target him.

events.title: Trump claims administration struck Venezuelan facility
events.summary: During an interview with Politico on December 26, Trump claimed that his administration "knocked out" what he described as a "big plant or big facility" in Venezuela, "where the ships come from." It was unclear what the president was talking about at the time, even to some Trump administration officials, as Zeteo reported. Trump also claimed the original plan to launch strikes in Nigeria was slated to take place earlier, but he directed them to "give them a Christmas present."
events.why_relevant: The president's vague and potentially false claims about military operations undermine transparency and informed public understanding of military actions; later reporting revealed the strike was conducted by the CIA on a dock with no confirmed casualties.
events.basis: During another interview, Trump potentially leaked new information by claiming that, on Wednesday, his administration 'knocked out' what he described as a 'big plant or big facility' in Venezuela, 'where the ships come from.

events.title: Trump administration sued Virginia over in-state tuition for undocumented students
events.summary: The Trump administration sued Virginia on December 29 over its policies allowing some undocumented students to pay in-state tuition, arguing the laws discriminate against US citizens. events.why_relevant: Federal litigation against state education policies targeting undocumented students represents executive overreach into state education authority and targets vulnerable children for exclusion from affordable education.

events.title: Trump welcomes Netanyahu to Mar-a-Lago and suggests pardon
events.summary: Trump welcomed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Mar-a-Lago on December 29, marking Netanyahu's fifth visit to the US since Trump's second term began in January. During the visit, Trump said he spoke to Israeli President Isaac Herzog and suggested a pardon is "on its way" for Netanyahu, who he called a "war-time prime minister." He also claimed without evidence that "more than half" of Gaza's population would leave the territory if given the opportunity. Netanyahu also awarded Trump the Israel Prize, making him its first non-Israeli recipient.
events.why_relevant: The president's suggestion of a pardon for a foreign leader facing legal proceedings represents potential abuse of pardon power for diplomatic favor; the award ceremony blurs lines between personal enrichment and official diplomacy.

events.title: Trump administration cuts UN funding by 88 percent
events.summary: The Trump administration made a significant cut to the amount of money the US has traditionally pledged to the UN on December 29, saying it would only contribute $2 billion, a massive drop from contributions in recent years that reached as high as $17 billion. Additionally, the administration warned UN agencies to "adapt, shrink, or die," with Secretary of State Marco Rubio tweeting that "this new model…will require the UN to cut bloat, remove duplication, and commit to powerful new impact, accountability, and oversight mechanisms."
events.why_relevant: Unilateral defunding of multilateral institutions undermines global cooperation on humanitarian, peacekeeping, and development issues; the move signals withdrawal from international commitments and reduces US diplomatic influence.
events.basis: The Trump administration made another significant cut to the amount of money the US has traditionally pledged to the UN, saying it would only contribute $2 billion, a massive drop from contributions in recent years that reached as high as $17 billion.

events.title: Federal judge blocks CFPB defunding effort
events.summary: A federal judge ruled on December 30 that the Trump administration can't move forward with efforts to defund the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), which is responsible for enforcing consumer financial laws and taking action against companies that violate those laws. The judge found the administration's legal argument to do so is "an unsupported and transparent attempt to starve the CFPB of funding and yet another attempt to achieve the very end the Court's injunction was put in place to prevent."
events.why_relevant: The court's protection of an independent agency's funding preserves its capacity to enforce consumer protections; the ruling constrains executive attempts to disable regulatory oversight through budgetary starvation.
events.basis: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration can't move forward with efforts to defund the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), which is responsible for enforcing consumer financial laws and taking action against companies that violate those laws.

events.why_relevant: The disclosure of DOJ leadership involvement in a selective prosecution decision undermines claims of prosecutorial independence and suggests political direction of law enforcement.

events.title: Trump administration freezes Minnesota childcare funds
events.summary: On Twitter, Deputy Health Secretary Jim O'Neill announced on December 30 that the Trump administration will freeze federal childcare funds to Minnesota in response to "blatant fraud that appears to be rampant" in the state and across the country, citing a right-wing influencer who claimed Somali residents operating daycares in Minneapolis committed up to $100 million in fraud. In response, Governor Tim Walz said the move was "Trump's long game," and that it's "been his plan all along."
events.why_relevant: Freezing childcare funds based on unsubstantiated claims from a right-wing influencer, targeting a specific ethnic community, constitutes weaponized federal funding cuts and discriminatory enforcement.

events.title: US military conducted strikes on three boats
events.summary: At the direction of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the US military conducted strikes against three boats on December 30, though it's unclear where the strikes took place. Later on Twitter, the US Southern Command said three people were killed in the first strike, while other targets "abandoned the other two vessels." The Intercept later reported that the US military actually killed 11 people in the boat strikes, bringing the total number of people killed in US strikes to 123.
events.why_relevant: Unilateral military strikes without congressional authorization, combined with discrepancies in casualty reporting, violate war powers and undermine transparency about military operations.

events.title: House Judiciary Committee releases Jack Smith testimony transcript
events.summary: The House Judiciary Committee released the transcript of former special counsel Jack Smith's testimony on December 31, during which he noted that "there is no historical analog for what President Trump did" in his efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election. Smith also said he was still considering indicting some of Trump's co-conspirators when he won the 2024 presidential election, and repeatedly denied there was any political interference in his investigation by the Biden administration to charge Trump.
events.why_relevant: Congressional release of special counsel testimony provides public record of the investigation into the president's efforts to overturn the 2020 election and refutes claims of political bias in the investigation.
events.basis: The House Judiciary Committee released the transcript of former special counsel Jack Smith's testimony delivered earlier this month, during which he noted that 'there is no historical analog for what President Trump did' in his efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election.

events.title: Federal appeals court orders return of California National Guard to governor
events.summary: A federal appeals court ordered the Trump administration to return control of hundreds of California National Guard troops to Governor Gavin Newsom on December 31. Meanwhile, Trump announced on Truth Social that he would be removing the National Guard from Chicago, Los Angeles, and Portland, following a Supreme Court ruling the week earlier that said he couldn't deploy troops to Chicago. However, Trump signaled he would be open to redeploying troops again, saying, "We will come back, perhaps in a much different and stronger form, when crime begins to soar again – Only a question of time!"
events.why_relevant: The court's order enforces federalism and state control over National Guard units; the president's threat to redeploy troops signals continued disregard for judicial authority and constitutional limits on executive power.
